stages.title: Measure before making
stages.description: Lock the design; verify the real room and a sample connector before ordering wood or drilling.
actions: Measure the ceiling height. The top crate envelope reaches about 2,442 mm; 2,630 mm is measured.
Measure the room width at three heights, both diagonals and the right-wall plumb. Record them, plus every socket, switch, radiator and pipe, in source/room-measurements.json.
Measure fitting seating stops, saddle height and screw positions using the measurement fields supplied with the model.
Check the independent right balcony leaf, gathered curtain, real clothes and the 600 mm minimum entrance with a physical mock-up.
Confirm wall construction, anchors and desk/shelf-arm/speaker load capacities. Choose fixings for the actual substrate.
notes: This is a checked geometry proposal, not a certified load rating or a drilling template. Do not cut the boards to these preview numbers until fitting measurements are entered.

stages.title: Lay out the kit
stages.description: Sort pipes by their printed catalog lengths, and keep similar-looking fittings separate.
actions: Use only the listed DOLLE PIPE family; do not mix generic plumbing threads or change a stock pipe length.
The BOM shows required pieces and purchase packs separately. Saddles and end covers come in packs of two.
Dry-fit one T/pipe/saddle/board connection. Check the end-cover fit; covers do not carry load.

There is no sliding fitting in this frame. Every post is built from the floor up as its own stack, and no two posts are joined by more than one threaded pipe, because a frame closed only by threads cannot be screwed together.
notes: A fitting is tightened to the direction it must face, not to the end of its thread, so most joints end slightly backed off. Use thread-locker on them, and follow the actual part instructions for torque.

stages.title: Stand the lower post stacks
stages.description: Lay out the ten main posts at their V18 positions and build each one up to desk height.
actions: Lay out paired front/back posts 290 mm apart, using the model axes rather than the wall surface as a datum.
Six posts start with 602 + coupling + 40 mm: the four desk posts, which take a cross next, and the pair beside the wardrobe. The four window-side posts start with a 150 mm tube and the shoe-shelf T.
Turn each T so its branch points along the wall toward its board (or into the room for a rail arm) before the next tube goes in.
Use floor protection under flanges and shim them level. Heights cannot be adjusted later; do not assume that a floor flange must be drilled into the rental floor.
notes: The near shelf frame is 50 mm before the desk edge frame used in older versions. Keep the V18 axes.

stages.title: Build the shared desk supports
stages.description: Four crosses at desk height: front arm, rear bridge and the wall fixing all sit on one line.
actions: Screw each 250 mm rear bridge into its middle and rear cross as a free piece first, then turn the lower post stacks up into the crosses.
From each middle cross a 250 mm arm runs to the front-leg elbow; the front leg is 602 + coupling + 40 mm. From each rear cross a 40 mm pipe runs into a wall flange under the back edge of the desktop.
There are no low braces. Each front leg is held only at its elbow, so check it for sideways play and keep heavy knocks off it.
The current fitting profile yields a 689 mm support-pipe axis. Keep all eight saddle screw points on the 704 mm underside plane.
notes: No separate short rear desk legs. The two front returns finish below the tabletop; no front-leg holes are required. Leave the final wall anchoring to the verified fixing specification.

materials.name: Four-way threaded cross
materials.sku: 96384 / EAN 4007557096384 — UNCONFIRMED: Bauhaus SE lists this EAN as a 4×3/4" corner coupling

stages.title: Fit the desktop and service shelf
stages.description: Keep the full 1,615 × 702 mm surface with a clear front edge.
actions: While the upper frame is still open, fit the desktop around the continuing rack posts and support it safely during assembly.

Transfer four post clearances from the measured frame. The preview uses 44 mm wide open-edge notches for all four, because a closed Ø44 bore would leave only 8 mm of timber to the edge. The two rear ones are corner notches.
Transfer the shallow underside tee/elbow reliefs from real castings. Do not break through the top face.
Round the entrance-side front corner to R100 mm. It widens the kitchen-corner passage; the nearest saddle screw stays on full-width timber.
Screw the desktop to its eight saddle tabs. Hang the 1615 × 230 × 18 mm rear service shelf on four separate wall shelf brackets at 500 mm underside / 518 mm top; it is not part of the pipe frame.

The service shelf begins 472 mm behind the front edge. Choose the brackets (about 200 mm reach) and their wall fixings for the real wall; the budget carries an allowance only. Cut its two rear post clearances as corner notches, transferred from actual parts, and keep the central knee area open.
notes: Preview top height: 732 mm. This is derived from stock lengths and unmeasured socket offsets; it may change after calibration.
Kitchen-corner passage in the model: 667 mm, limited by the low front brace on the near leg rather than the desk corner. Keep at least 600 mm.

stages.title: Complete the upper posts
stages.description: Carry on up each post: tube, fitting, tube, until the top fitting closes it.
actions: Follow the stack list for each post exactly; the tube between two fittings sets the shelf spacing. Do not shorten a tube or leave one partly threaded to adjust a height.
Shelf lines land at 1,044 / 1,484 / 1,824 mm underside and the top boards at 2,164 mm, the same on the desk side and the wardrobe side.
Posts end in a fitting, not a cover: an elbow at the two ends of the run and a T laid on its side where boards meet on both sides.
Keep the frame supported until the boards and wall ties are on. Without its boards nothing ties the front posts to the rear posts.

stages.title: Tie the frame to the wall
stages.description: One flange per rear post, plus the two at desk height.
actions: Each rear post has a T facing the wall at 1,909 mm with a 40 mm pipe into a flange. The desk posts have a second flange at 689 mm.
Nothing is fixed to the wall between 150 and 450 mm above the floor, where sockets and their feeds usually run. Check the wall with a cable detector anyway before drilling.
Each post stands 75 mm off the wall in front of its flange, so plan hex-head screws and a spanner, or a stubby ratchet. Pack out behind a flange where the wall is not straight.
Keep the bar and kitchen fixed. Confirm the kitchen-corner passage is about 667 mm in the actual flat.
notes: Wall material and permissible fixings remain to be verified. The model does not specify an anchor type or allowable structural load.

stages.title: Add the two short-clothes rows
stages.description: The entrance-side wardrobe bay keeps two levels of short hanging storage.
actions: Screw the upper 1,000 mm rail at 1,909 mm between the Ts on the two front posts.

The lower rail at 929 mm hangs from the two rear posts on 200 mm arms and elbows, 50 mm behind the front post line. A second rail between the same front posts would close a threaded loop that cannot be assembled.
Join each rail to one post first, then turn the neighbouring post stack onto it.
Check real short garments on both rows; the heights are fixed by the stock tubes.

stages.title: Keep a full-length coat drop
stages.description: The window-side bay uses the next smaller 602 mm stock rail.
actions: Fit the 602 mm coat rail at 1,909 mm.
Allow about 70 mm hanger drop and up to 1,500 mm garment length in the design envelope.
Four positions at roughly 140 mm pitch are shown; bulky winter coats may need fewer places.
Keep the curtain gathered and the right balcony door/handle sweep clear.
notes: The coat-bay width is a stock-pipe decision, not a cut-down 802 mm rail.

stages.title: Add the shelf arms
stages.description: Every board rests on four 250 mm arms, one from each corner post.
actions: Screw a 250 mm arm into each T branch that points along the wall. The arms are cantilevers; nothing joins a front post to a rear post except the boards.
Where two boards meet at one post and one height, the top fitting has a socket on each side.
Fit the saddle tabs on the arms with the tabs pointing inward, toward the middle of the board.
Do not hang weight on an arm before its board is screwed on.
notes: No load rating for these cantilever arms has been established. A saddle holder wraps around a horizontal pipe; the arm, its thread and the T carry the load.

stages.title: Build the folded-clothes stack
stages.description: Four intermediate boards leave usable spaces for folded pullovers.
actions: Set the 580 × 350 × 28 mm boards at underside heights 704, 1,044, 1,484 and 1,824 mm.
Use four saddle tabs per board, one on each arm; transfer screw positions from the actual hardware.
Keep the paired folded stacks inside the shelf depth.
Clear openings between the boards are 312 / 412 / 312 / 312 mm; the highest front opening is 40 mm less behind the light lip.

stages.title: Cap the storage bays with wood
stages.description: The three top boards finish at 2,192 mm, before the crates.
actions: Fit the 978 mm top over short hanging and the two 580 mm tops over folds and long coats.
Use four saddle tabs per board, one on each arm.
Keep the front edge clear for the removable light covers.
Top crates reach about 2,442 mm, 188 mm below the measured 2,630 mm ceiling; check the actual top shelf with a crate before loading it.

stages.title: Fit the low coat-bay shelf
stages.description: The long coats retain a low shoe shelf rather than a second hanging row.
actions: Fit the 580 × 350 × 28 mm board at 200 mm underside height.
Screw it to its four saddle holders.
The preview allows 100 mm shoes above the 228 mm top; verify actual boots and coat hems.
Keep the door-side area free of loose shoes and trailing garments.

stages.title: Build the three desk shelves
stages.description: The overhead shelves reuse the same main frame as the desk and wardrobe.
actions: Fit the 1,528 × 350 mm boards at underside heights 1,484, 1,824 and 2,164 mm.
The lowest board is 40 mm thick for the proposed MITTLED pocket; the upper two are 28 mm.
Each long board takes eight saddle tabs, two on each of its four arms.
Do not route the light pocket until clips, plugs, cable access and suitability of recessed installation are confirmed.
notes: The proposed 1,320 × 32 × 20 mm underside pocket is unverified. Surface-mounting the original IKEA clips behind a removable wood lip is the alternative.

stages.title: Float the speakers inside the shelf column
stages.description: Two side arms per tray; the trays sit between the middle and rear posts, so nothing overhangs the desktop.
actions: Attach each tray to two uncut 250 mm arms, each screwed into a T on its own upright.
Fit four saddle holders per 370 × 370 × 25 mm tray. The trays are square to the frame, flush with the shelf fronts, and mirrored about the desk centre line.

Tray top: 1,069 mm. Turn each speaker about 42° on its tray so it faces the seated ear reference (x 2,620, z 1,220 mm), not the seat centre. 370 mm is the smallest square that takes the turned speaker with a 5 mm edge margin.
Each speaker sits centred on its tray, fully supported, at least 15 mm from the nearest frame part. The speakers end up about 1,123 mm apart and 32 mm from the wall.
Tilt each speaker about 9.54° down on angled isolation pads.
Check real speaker weight, tweeter height and screw retention before loading.
notes: No load rating for this cantilever arrangement has been established. The desk-end placement gives a wide stereo angle, not a calibrated monitor triangle.

stages.title: Give worn clothes their own rail
stages.description: The throw-over rail marks clothes that are worn but ready to wear again.
actions: Use the two 100 mm returns, the two elbows and the 602 mm rail shown in the graph.
The rail sits at 1,369 mm in front of the folded bay.
Keep the draped item in the front 200 mm zone, y=3,950–4,150 mm.
Leave the rear part toward the balcony clear so the door handle cannot catch clothing.

stages.title: Close the arm ends and recheck joints
stages.description: Cap the open arm ends once every board is screwed on.
actions: Fit the listed end covers on the shelf arms after confirming their actual fit on this DOLLE thread family.
Recheck every threaded joint for direction and thread-locker, and every wall tie and saddle screw.
Treat caps as covers only, never as load-bearing connections.
Remove temporary support only after the boards, wall ties and desk fixing checks are complete.

stages.title: Light the work surface
stages.description: Keep the two original MITTLED bars intact.
actions: Use two 600 mm MITTLED units with their original mounting clips and compatible leads/driver.
The proposed pocket must retain at least 20 mm timber above it, with access for clips and connectors.
If recess suitability or service clearance cannot be verified, surface-mount behind a removable wood lip.
Route low-voltage leads away from clothes and sharp edges. Keep drivers accessible; do not enclose mains equipment in a routed pocket.
notes: Two 5.5 W MITTLED bars draw 11 W together on their own compatible driver. No LED strip is shortened.

stages.title: Hide the upper shelf lighting
stages.description: Warm light comes from intact ÖVERSIDAN bars behind removable oak covers.
actions: Use one 960 mm, two 460 mm and four 710 mm ÖVERSIDAN bars across the five upper lighting positions.
Use original surface clips inside the open-back wood cover: 18 × 40 mm front lip, 37 × 12 mm return, and removable end cheeks.
Leave access to the screws, connectors and seven intact 3.5 m fixture leads.
Connect the seven bars to the separate 30 W driver: 23.2 W total. Use ON mode for open shelves, rather than relying on wardrobe-door AUTO.
notes: Housing cross sections, clip offsets, local wood reliefs and cable access remain preview dimensions. Keep the existing main ceiling fixture off for the modeled night scene.

stages.title: Add the six crates and equipment
stages.description: Finish the storage without changing the locked layout.
actions: Place four KNAGGLIG 460 × 310 × 250 mm crates on top and two stacked in the lower folded bay.
Check that top crates can be lifted out below the measured ceiling and secure storage as appropriate.
Fit the reused monitor on the optional desk-clamp VESA arm at the desktop rear edge; no monitor stand fits behind the 61-key controller. Keep the clamp jaw clear of the router antennas.

Put the M1 Mac mini, router, and the router and dock power supplies on the rear service shelf; leave its front/back open and Mac ports facing along the shelf. The Mac mini M1 has an internal power supply, so the third brick bay is spare.

Fit the Focusrite and OWC dock beneath opposite front ends using adjustable open U holders. Keep front sockets/knobs accessible and preserve the central 700 mm knee width. Exact Focusrite generation and holder model remain unconfirmed.
Secure individual bricks without covering vents; route audio away from the brick bay and retain cable service loops. Check plug bend space and short tabletop screw lengths.
The shown dock-to-Mac route needs a 2 m certified Thunderbolt lead allowance; the supplied 0.8 m dock cable will not follow this route. Remove the cable allowance if you already own a suitable lead.
Keep the kitchen and bar fixed and use removable finishes. The TV is not part of this layout.
extra: Reused M1 Mac mini, router, OWC dock and two-input Focusrite
Two adjustable under-desk device holder sets (allowance)
Removable equipment straps and cable clips

stages.title: Walk through the real room
stages.description: A physical fit check completes the concept review.
actions: Walk the entrance with the chair parked and in use. Preserve at least 600 mm; the modelled kitchen-corner passage is 667 mm.
Open the independent right balcony leaf and check its handle, curtains, coats and worn-clothes rail.
Confirm all doors, drawers and the fixed bar remain usable. The bar has only 240 mm of leg recess.
Test the dimmers and cable access. Check load-bearing fixings with the appropriate installer before loading storage or leaning on the desk.
notes: The public model shows concept geometry and artistically balanced lighting, not a structural or lux certification. The bathroom is only a shell because its fixtures are unknown.
